# Non-vacuity meta-gate exemption list (scripts/lib/gate-vacuity.sh).
#
# Generated by measurement (testing doctrine v2, P1b), not guessed: every
# tests/test-*.sh file was run and checked for at least one line matching
# `^PASS:`/`^FAIL:` (colon-prefixed, start-of-line) in its stdout — the
# shared pass()/fail() helper most files use, or an equivalent inline
# echo. 77 of 91 files conform. These 14 do not, in two shapes:
#   bracket-format    — the file DOES report per-assertion results, but in
#                        the repo's older `[PASS]`/`[FAIL]` bracket style,
#                        not the colon protocol the lib counts.
#   silent-success     — the file's pass counter (often an `ok()` helper)
#                        increments silently and only echoes on failure
#                        (`FAIL: ...`), so a fully-passing run emits ZERO
#                        PASS:/FAIL: lines — genuinely vacuous under the
#                        strict protocol today, not a measurement miss.
#   opt-in-live        — the file is a manual, opt-in gate guarded by an
#                        env switch (it drives real, paid model sessions).
#                        With the switch off it prints only SKIP and
#                        asserts nothing, which is correct behaviour, not
#                        a defect; its static coverage lives in a sibling
#                        suite. Unlike the two shapes above this is not a
#                        retrofit candidate — there is nothing to convert.
# Neither of the first two shapes is rewritten as part of this build (retrofit fails closed,
# no day-one false-positive wave); each is a candidate for a follow-up
# pass()/fail() conversion.
#
# Format: one path per line, relative to repo root, optional " # reason".
